studies.reason: Brief exclusions and protocol inclusion 5: the Methods admit only patients who completed at least a 2-year follow-up, so Tab2 holds the 97 of 204 treated patients (one eye each) seen at 24 months, its last visit, a complete-case set (the kept case is a minimum follow-up shorter than the last tabulated visit). Tab4 is a further complete-case subset of the same eyes (31 eyes seen at 36 months), a nested cohort under addendum 1.

Protocol inclusion 5: only eyes judged refractively stable at 4 and 6 months after CXL were eligible for the ICL that defines the cohort, and eyes with any later corneal surgery were excluded (Methods 2.1), so the group is selected by a post-treatment outcome. In addition, the post-ICL columns of tab1 have no exact time since CXL (ICL 'at least 6 months after CXL', Methods 2.3) and tab2 is a 10-eye complete-case subset.

Brief exclusions (the brief's own example): medsci-11-00043-t002 reports only the 35 eyes with a full 10-year follow-up out of 886 treated eyes (Results), a complete-case set; the 3-year Kmax of the 610-eye subgroup appears only in the text, and t001 gives the baseline only.

Brief exclusions and protocol inclusion 5: inclusion required regular follow-up at 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 years and excluded incomplete follow-up and any later corneal surgery (Methods 'Patients'; Results: 89 of 272 conventionally treated eyes), so T2 is a complete-case set that also drops eyes needing a second procedure, while repeat-CXL eyes stay inside the group.

Brief exclusions: the 46 eyes are a subgroup of all consecutive CXL patients of 2007-2011, restricted by inclusion criterion to a complete keratometry set at baseline and years 7, 9 and 12 (Methods), exactly the visits of jcm-14-02585-t001, so the table is a complete-case set.

Protocol 'Values, times and identities': the only postoperative Kmax-t (tbl2) is at a follow-up whose time is given only as a per-cohort mean ± SD (Methods 'Data Collection'; tbl2 R5), not as a visit time, so it cannot be converted to months exactly and only the baseline remains. Kmax-t is also an in-house maximum of a recomputed tangential-curvature map (Methods 'Corneal Geometry Analysis'), not the topographer's Kmax.

Brief exclusions: only eyes with at least 6-month results at the clinic were included because many treated patients lacked follow-up (Materials and Methods), and 6 months is the only postoperative visit of t0001, so the 27 eyes are a complete-case set (a minimum follow-up equal to, not shorter than, the last tabulated visit).

The scleral-lens group is out of scope (brief: scleral lenses alone). The untreated matched control group of medicina-61-00728-t002 was drawn only from patients required to have at least one year of follow-up data (Methods 2.1), equal to the only tabulated follow-up at 12 months, so it is a complete-case set chosen retrospectively (protocol inclusion 5; brief exclusions).

Brief exclusions: only patients with at least 3 years of postoperative follow-up were included and shorter follow-up was excluded (Methods; section 2.1), and 3 years is the last visit of jcm-14-07141-t003, so both groups (32 and 30 eyes) are complete-case sets; the outcome is also described as the last visit after 3 years (section 2.6).

Protocol inclusion 1: the rows of t1-opth-8-1435 labelled maximum keratometry are, per the Results, the steep keratometry (written 'steep keratometry (Kmax)' and paired with flat keratometry 'Kmin'), i.e. steep-meridian K, which is not Kmax; no other table reports Kmax.

No binding rule excludes t0003: Kmax (Pentacam, dioptres per t0001) as mean ± SD at Preop and yearly to 7 years for the consecutive S-CXL (93 eyes) and A-CXL (90 eyes) groups in columns C11 and C12, rows R3-R10. Before a record is built, a label conflict must be resolved or recorded: t0001 R13 and the Results text assign the baseline and the decrease printed under S-CXL in t0003 to A-CXL, so the procedure context of each Kmax column depends on which printed label is correct.

Brief exclusions: only records of eyes with at least 2 years of follow-up were reviewed and eyes with shorter follow-up were excluded (Patients and Methods), and month 24 is the last visit of t0002, so the 21 eyes are a complete-case set.

Brief exclusions: aos17551-tbl-0002 (and its regrouping tbl-0004) gives baseline and 1-year Kmax only for the eyes seen at 1 year (24 and 26 eyes at both visits) of 27 randomised per arm, with patients lost to follow-up (Abstract; Results, Figure 1), so each arm is a complete-case set. tbl-0005 holds only the eyes that met the treatment-failure criterion (outcome-selected, protocol inclusion 5).

Brief exclusions: Tab2 gives preoperative, 6- and 18-month maximum keratometry only for the 28 eyes per group seen at 18 months, out of 30 enrolled per group (Methods; Results), so both groups are complete-case sets rather than whole groups with attrition.

Brief exclusions: IJO_2778_21-t001 covers only the 19 of the original 25 eyes that returned at 5 years (Results), a complete-case set; IJO_2778_21-t002 gives only changes for the baseline-Kmax subgroups without their own baselines (protocol inclusion 4).
